tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise Matt Dobbs, local teacher at Glen Innes High School on being honoured with the Prime Minister's Prize for Excellence in Science Teaching in Secondary Schools, in the 2025 Prime Minister's Prizes for Science. Such is the importance of this honour, prizes at these awards are considered Australia's most prestigious and highly regarded Science awards. I congratulate Matt on this outstanding and well-deserved accolade, with his excellence recognised for his many achievements, including: inspiring students with his unwavering commitment to science, technology, engineering and mathematics [STEM] education; going beyond to engage students and mentor teachers in his school and nationwide; promoting STEM to students from a range of backgrounds and teaching students from remote communities of NSW. I commend Matt on his creative teaching methods, extra-curricular activities around science, and for continuing to develop and share his knowledge with others. I thank Matt for his dedication to his students and the school community of Glen Innes High School. Matt's valuable contribution to enriching young people's lives in our community is greatly appreciated.

tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —Each year the Castle Hill & District RSL Sub-Branch select students to be Anzac Ambassadors. The Ambassadors are taught public speaking, and they research a set subject to present at various commemorations throughout the year. The Castle Hill RSL Sub-Branch Secondary School Ambassador Program began in 2015. The Ambassadors each spoke on Anzac Day at the Anzac Ceremony at Centenary of Anzac Reserve, Castle Hill, Remembrance Day at the Ceremony held on 9 November 2025 at the Balcombe Heights Estate and finally at the Remembrance Day Ceremony held on 11 November 2025 at the Castle Hill RSL Club. This year the Anzac Ambassadors were Ella Dickson (Crestwood High), Harry McMahon (Rouse Hill High), Isaac Browne (Castle Hill High) and Ashlyn Kumar (Oakhill College). I was present at each Ceremony, and I wish to recognise and commend each Ambassador on the respectful manner that each Ambassador brought to the role of Anzac Ambassador. I also acknowledge the Castle Hill & District RSL Club for continuing the Anzac Ambassador Program. I also thank Bryan Mullan and David Hand for their continuing role in the Ambassador Program.

tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I ask the House to join me in thanking Riley Pengilly, School Captain of Epping Boys High School, for his outstanding contribution to the 2025 Ryde Remembrance Day Service. Riley took on the important role of Master of Ceremonies at this year's commemoration, which brought together veterans, families, and local community members to honour those who served and sacrificed in defence of our nation. As MC, Riley demonstrated poise, leadership and respect beyond his years. His role was pivotal in setting the tone for what was a solemn, reflective and dignified ceremony. I commend Riley for the maturity and presence he brought to this occasion. Remembrance Day holds deep meaning for many in our community, particularly for the families of our veterans. It was heartening to see a young leader like Riley rise to the occasion with such care and thoughtfulness. His contribution reflected a broader spirit of respect and civic pride among our youth, which is encouraging to witness. I thank Riley once again for his efforts and commend Epping Boys High School for continuing to instill a strong sense of service and responsibility in its students.

tree_branches.text: Ms KAREN McKEOWN ( Penrith ) —Congratulations to Lucinda Harvey, the founder and driving force behind Saving True Blues Charity on a successful fundraising event recently held at Penrith Paceway. Lucinda's commitment to mental health awareness, community engagement, and advocacy demonstrates her outstanding leadership. Lucinda founded 'Saving True Blues' to raise awareness for suicide and mental health. What began as a local initiative has now expanded into a state-wide movement. Lucinda's innovative approach involves organising 4-wheel-driving and camping weekends, providing a platform for individuals to step out of their comfort zones, explore nature, and engage in crucial conversations about mental health. We know that mental health is one of the most important challenges facing our community today. Behind every statistic is a person: a mate, a partner, a son or daughter, a colleague, or a neighbour. And far too often, those who are struggling the most feel like they have to do it alone. That's why initiatives like Saving True Blues are so important. They remind us that strength isn't about silence. It's about reaching out and showing up for one another. It's about creating spaces where people feel seen, heard, and supported. What matters is that those conversations happen. Penrith is proud.

tree_branches.text: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA ( Drummoyne ) —I rise to acknowledge a local Rhodes resident and author, Dr Uma Srinivasan and to sincerely congratulate her on the launch of her new book 'Etched in Gold'. Etched in Gold is a historical fiction, telling the story of two Indian women connected through their passion for music and their culture throughout the 16th to 18th centuries. The novel is an important reminder of the power of storytelling in sharing histories and preserving cultural heritage. Prior to beginning her journey as an author, Dr Srinivasan worked as a computer scientist, obtaining her PhD from the University of New South Wales. Her transition to literature is a testament to her talent and dedication to lifelong learning. I have known Dr Srinivasan for a number of years during her time serving on the City of Canada Bay Council's Rhodes Community Committee, where she volunteered her time serving Rhodes and working to bring better services for the community. I sincerely congratulate Dr Srinivasan on the release of her novel 'Etched in Gold' and I wish her all the very best.

tree_branches.text: Mr RAY WILLIAMS ( Kellyville ) —I'm pleased to recognise the 10-year anniversary of the Hills Football Association, an organisation whose roots were laid well before its 2015 formation and 2016 launch. A dedicated local association became necessary when thousands of Hills players were travelling over 30 kilometres away each Saturday, instead of within their own community. Today, over 16,000 players take part in Hills Football competitions close to home. First formed as the Sydney Hills Football Association, it launched with more than 8,000 registered players. The founding clubs included Baulkham Hills FC, Castle Hill RSL Rockets, Castle Hill United, Hills Grammar, Hills Knights, Kellyville United, North Rocks Soccer Club, North West FC, Norwest Cougars and Rouse Hill Rangers. Renamed the Hills Football Association, its inaugural committee Graeme Luck, Matthew Perram, Craig Gough, Suzan Torville, Dino DiGulio, William Renton and Mick Pawelko worked tirelessly to shape the strong organisation we see today, now home to over twice the original number of clubs and players. Next year, Hills Football will become a formalised "Association Zone'' under Football NSW after nine years as an affiliate. I thank all who supported its growth, including the Hills Shire Council and former GM Dave Walker.

tree_branches.text: Ms ELENI PETINOS ( Miranda ) —I celebrate 90 remarkable years of the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch and its enduring service to our community. In 1935, returned servicemen Bill Luxton and Alex Porter recognised the need for a place where veterans could reconnect with those who understood their experiences. Their call for a meeting at the Miranda School of Arts led to the formation of the Miranda Sub-Branch - a place that nurtured camaraderie through some of Australia's most challenging decades. From its humble beginnings, the Sub-Branch grew into a supportive home offering welfare assistance, social connection, and a library dedicated to preserving military history. Today, it proudly marks nine decades of honouring service, supporting veterans, and strengthening community ties. To commemorate this extraordinary milestone, the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch hosted a 90th anniversary luncheon on 9 November, bringing together ex-servicemen, families, and friends to share stories, memories, and fellowship. I recognise Steve Bull, Joanne Beavis, Warren Barnes OAM, Alan Lark, Reverend Jennie Everist, Greg Beavis, Shane Hall, Jim Lowe and Bruce Grill for their contributions to this special occasion. Ninety years on, the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch stands as a testament to resilience, mateship and unwavering commitment to our veterans.

I recognise Steve Bull, Joanne Beavis, Warren Barnes OAM, Alan Lark, Reverend Jennie Everist, Greg Beavis, Shane Hall, Jim Lowe and Bruce Grill for their contributions to this special occasion. Ninety years on, the Miranda RSL Sub-Branch stands as a testament to resilience, mateship and unwavering commitment to our veterans.

tree_branches.text: Ms DONNA DAVIS ( Parramatta ) —I was delighted to join the community on Saturday 1st November for Foundation Day, celebrating Parramatta's proud history and heritage. This year Foundation Day was held at Hambledon Cottage, providing an opportunity to introduce this State heritage listed site to a wider audience as families, friends and even a few four-legged locals enjoyed the free family event. Foundation Day marks the arrival of Governor Arthur Phillip in Parramatta on 2 November 1788 and the start of agricultural projects in the area. The date has traditionally been celebrated with large civic events, street carnivals and parades. In more recent years the actual day has become less of a focus than the sharing of Parramatta's heritage and stories. This year visitors enjoyed guided tours of Hambledon Cottage, horse drawn carriage rides, weaving and blacksmith demonstrations, roving entertainment, children's workshops, face painting an animal farm and entertainment from the Parramatta's City Band. Congratulations to the Parramatta and Districts Historical Society, the City of Parramatta, the Parramatta Lions Club and all who were involved in making the day a success.

tree_branches.text: Ms KOBI SHETTY ( Balmain ) —I would like to recognise the Associazione Napoletana, a vibrant community of local Italians, who come together each month to share their love of food, culture, and friendship. These monthly gatherings celebrate not only the rich culinary traditions of Naples and southern Italy, but also the warmth and generosity of a community that welcomes everyone to enjoy great company and great food. Italian culture is woven into the heart of Leichhardt, shaping the character of our community, strengthening and enriching the lives of community members and visitors alike. I had the pleasure of attending this month's dinner and got to experience the delight this organisation brings to the community. Thank you to the President Michele Fezza and his wife Susanna Fezza, Vice President Carmine Charley Telese, Director Carmine Zarrella, Secartary Franca De Francesco, Treasurer Salvatore Rizzo, Giovanna Cardamone, the executive director of Italian welfare group ItSoWel in Wollongong, Luisa Perugini and all those involved in Associazione Napoletana for fostering friendship, community and tradition in Leichhardt, and thank you for having me at this month's dinner, it was an absolute delight.

tree_branches.text: Mr PHILIP DONATO ( Orange ) —David Farrell aged 83 from my electorate, is a man who embodies the true spirit of small country communities. Mr Farrell was recently recognised for his extraordinary commitment to his community through his involvement with the Cudal-Cargo Lions Club for more than 40 years. He was awarded the prestigious Melvin Jones Fellowship as an acknowledgement of more than four decades of his service to the community through a number of projects to enhance the quality of life of district residents. During his years of service to the club, Mr Farrell has held every executive role from president, to secretary and treasurer and only recently decided to step back from the role of treasurer at the club. He is a valued member of the community who first came the town as a Postmaster 40 years ago and became immediately invested in giving back by becoming involved in the process of the inaugural committee for the formation of the Cudal-Cargo Lions Club. During his time of service to the club, Mr Farrell has over seen the donation of $50,000 to Cancer Care Western NSW as well as a strong involvement with the formation of the Cudal and Cargo Men's Sheds.

tree_branches.text: Ms KATELIN McINERNEY ( Ki ama ) —I would like to recognise Mark Burns, the founder of The Man Walk, for his outstanding contribution to men's health and wellbeing in our community and across Australia. Beginning in Kiama in 2019, Mark launched a simple idea with powerful intent: to create a space where men could walk, talk, and support one another without judgement. Since then, The Man Walk has grown to over 80 locations nationwide, with more than 130,000 men taking part. Through Mark's leadership, thousands of men have found connection, routine, mateship, and a safe place to speak openly about the challenges they face. Countless participants credit The Man Walk with improving their mental health, building lasting friendships, and, in some cases, changing or even saving lives. Mark's vision has sparked a movement rooted in compassion and community strength. We thank him for walking alongside so many and for inspiring a culture of reaching out for support.

tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —Congratulations to Varley Group on its induction into the Hunter Manufacturing Awards Hall of Fame. This achievement recognises nearly 140 years of innovation and craftsmanship in the Hunter region. Founded in 1886, Varley is one of Newcastle's oldest and most respected companies, a large local employer, and national leader across the defence, emergency services, marine, health, cyber, and mining sectors. This honour celebrates Varley's remarkable ability to evolve and diversify while keeping its headquarters and heart firmly in the Hunter. The company's commitment to apprenticeships, veterans' employment, and STEM education, through partnerships with local schools, TAFE NSW, and the University of Newcastle, continues to shape the next generation of manufacturing talent. Employing more than 1,200 people across 12 facilities, Varley's impact extends well beyond its projects. It stands as a symbol of Hunter ingenuity, adaptability, and pride in building things that matter. Congratulations to the entire Varley team on this prestigious recognition and for continuing to define what world-class manufacturing looks like, in Newcastle and right across the Hunter.

tree_branches.text: Mr DAVID LAYZELL ( Upper Hunter ) —I want to acknowledge the ongoing work in the Upper Hunter to improve road safety starting with our newest road users. Upper Hunter Shire Council and Hunter Valley Police District began the Learner Night Driver Program in late-2024 and it is being strongly supported by the community. Hunter Learner Night Drive is for learner drivers of any age, who must be accompanied by an appropriately licenced supervisor aged over 25. The event exposes learner drivers to real life driving scenarios and the opportunity to interact with police in a controlled environment. Learner drivers use a track at Scone Airport and get to experience stationary and mobile breath tests with police as well as receiving advice and guidance on how to safely undertake these tasks. The track includes a section where drivers can practice reverse parallel parking, roadcraft and vehicle manoeuvring. Learner Night Drive is supported by Hunter Valley Highway Patrol, Transport for NSW, NSW Ambulance, Singleton Council, Muswellbrook Shire Council and Merriwa VRA. I also want to acknowledge the corporate supporters assisting this initiative including JBS Scone, Bengalla Mining Company, Pays Air Service and Hunter Warbirds.

tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) —I would like to celebrate the unveiling of the Pauline Menzcer Statue at South Bondi. From humble beginnings at Bondi, Pauline became our very own ASP world champion. Along the way she became known for her refined surfing style, valiant big wave approach and hilarious antics at post contest parties. She was, after all, known by friends as "naughty Pauls". Pauline's story – including her ability to overcome personal adversity – and significant health issues – were detailed in the movie "Girls Can't Surf". And it was the Director of that movie- Chris Nelius - who has been the driving force behind the statue –from concept to permissions and funding. Chris points out that only 6% of statues in this country are of women. There are more statues of animals. So now there's one more – to honour Pauline's legacy and inspire the next generation of young women and men to follow their dreams.

tree_branches.text: Ms LIESL TESCH ( Gosford ) —Our 2025 Gosford Community Champion Award recipients have blown me away with their kindness, passion and generosity. I would like to acknowledge Lisa Caswell, an incredible woman who has ignited community spirit in many of us while showcasing kindness and bringing smiles to our vulnerable community members. Lisa has dedicated her time at Meals on Wheels Central Coast for several years to help our community members feel safe and independent and well fed. Being the kind spirit Lisa is, she always makes the clients happy when they received their meals from her. From the light-hearted chat to the caring actions, Lisa has provided more than just food because to some of these community members, seeing Lisa might be the best thing happened in their week. Meals on Wheels is an important organisation on the Central Coast and with people like Lisa, who have been modelling true community champion that make Meals on Wheels extra special to our community. I thank the fabulous Lisa Caswell for her compassion and kindness towards the Meals on Wheels community.

Lisa has dedicated her time at Meals on Wheels Central Coast for several years to help our community members feel safe and independent and well fed. Being the kind spirit Lisa is, she always makes the clients happy when they received their meals from her. From the light-hearted chat to the caring actions, Lisa has provided more than just food because to some of these community members, seeing Lisa might be the best thing happened in their week. Meals on Wheels is an important organisation on the Central Coast and with people like Lisa, who have been modelling true community champion that make Meals on Wheels extra special to our community. I thank the fabulous Lisa Caswell for her compassion and kindness towards the Meals on Wheels community.

tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minister for Roads ) —Mr Austin was a respected leader and quintessential gentleman - a pillar of the Maitland community, where his wisdom and wit shaped headlines and lives for decades. Born in Singleton, his early years were shaped by resilience. Mr Austin attended Francis Xavier Catholic Primary School and Singleton High School. His formal education was cut short at age 14, despite winning a scholarship to Marist Brothers Maitland. At 20, Mr Austin made a bold career switch, leaving a secure railway job to become a journalist, hired as a B-grade journalist at the Singleton Argus. His dedication was legendary: to master his craft, he learnt shorthand, and famously read a dictionary from A-Z, devoured a Roget's Thesaurus, and systematically worked his way through a 20-volume encyclopedia, all to build his vocabulary and general knowledge. Mr Austin worked at the Singleton Argus, founded the Cessnock Advertiser, moved to the The Mercury, The Manning River Times, returning to be Editor of The Maitland Mercury, ultimately serving as the managing editor-in-chief for Rural Press, overseeing approximately 180 country newspapers across Australia. VALE Mr Austin and thank you for your service to so many communities.

tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —On Monday 10 November, I had the pleasure of addressing the 2025 Model Global Parliament at the Parliament of New South Wales. The Model Global Parliament, an initiative of the Institute for Global Peace and Sustainable Governance, gives students the opportunity to experience a simulated global parliament and debate real-world issues, developing their decision-making and leadership skills. I was deeply impressed by how thoughtfully the students engaged with complex global challenges and proposed constructive, compassionate solutions. It was wonderful to see them demonstrate such enthusiasm and insight. I recognise Dr Zeny Edwards OAM for all her work in bringing students together and helping them reach their full potential. The work you do is life changing.

tree_branches.text: Mr MICHAEL KEMP ( Oxley ) —What an outstanding effort from Dorrigo High School's very own Brydi Fittock, who recently represented her school and community with pride at the Inter-Schools Horse Extravaganza (ISHE) in Tamworth. Brydi and her horse, Sarah Fene Raine, took to the arena in the dressage and senior 60cm show jumping events, competing against talented riders from schools right across the state. It's no small feat stepping into such a high-pressure competition, but Brydi showed incredible composure and determination, achieving an impressive third place after jumping a clear round in both Round 1 and the jump off! Representing Dorrigo High on a stage like ISHE is about more than just results. It's about courage, commitment, and the passion that drives young people like Brydi to give their best, even when the stakes are high and the nerves are real. Her success is a wonderful reflection of the strong community spirit that defines Dorrigo, where hard work, teamwork and a love for horses run deep. Congratulations, Brydi, on this fantastic achievement. You've made your school, your community, and everyone back home incredibly proud.

tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker, I would like to recognise Anne Elliott who has been awarded the 2025 JR Muller Award for Promotion and Marketing by Gliding Australia. Each year Gliding Australia take the opportunity to celebrate individuals who lift the sport higher though dedication, innovation and service. Those whose contributions ensure the community continues to thrive. Anne has earned a reputation for celebrating gliding with passion and consistency. She is an administrator of multiple gliding Facebook pages where shares daily stories, news and historical treasures with both Australian and international audiences. Her engaging posts help broaden the reach of Gliding Australia, sparking enthusiasm for the sport among pilots and non-pilots alike. This is not the first time Anne's outstanding work in promoting gliding has been recognised, she was also the winner of this award in 2009, further highlighting her enduring talent and passion for the sport. Locally, Anne is a dedicated and passionate member and Patron of the Narromine Aero Club. A true community gem, when she is not promoting and sharing her love of gliding, she lends her time and expertise to other local organisations such as Narromine Cottage Craft. Congratulations Anne on this well-deserved recognition!

tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Minister for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Coast ) —I WISH to congratulate Richmond Riverkeeper Kristin den Exter who was named winner of the Local Hero category at the 2025 NSW Coastal Conference Awards in Ballina recently. Kristin was recognised for her outstanding contribution to river health, community consultation, and coastal care. The award acknowledges Kristin's leadership through Richmond Riverkeeper and the Richmond RiverFest, a month-long celebration of culture, community and Country that connects people from the sea to the source. I have followed the work of the Richmond Riverkeepers closely and receive regular updates from them. Associate Professor in History at Southern Cross University and fellow Richmond Riverkeeper Adele Wessell told The Lismore App: "Kristen has been listening to what the river is telling us her whole life, listing to the knowledge of Custodians and First Peoples and committing herself to a lifetime of working with the river with integrity and love in a way that inspires everyone around her," Associate Professor Wessell said. For her part, Kristen spoke of collective effort: "From Elders and artists to scientists and volunteers, we're all working together so that the rivers of the Richmond catchment can one day be drinkable, swimmable and fishable again."

tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH COOKE ( Cootamundra ) —Congratulations to the Cowra Golf Club and Julie and Mark Tucker for hosting another hugely successful Jersey Golf Day event to raise awareness for organ and tissue donation. Participants were encouraged to wear their favourite sports jersey as part of the National Jersey Day Organ Donation Awareness initiative, combining community spirit, sport, and an important message about the gift of life. Julie and Mark Tucker have shown remarkable strength and compassion following the unimaginable loss of their beloved son, Brady, in 2021. Through their grief and inspired by Brady's love of golf and his selfless act of organ donation, they have dedicated themselves to increasing awareness about the importance and life-changing impact of organ donation. This annual event continues to grow each year, showcasing the Cowra and golfing communities' generosity, unity, and commitment to supporting meaningful causes. I extend my congratulations to all who helped organise the day and to everyone who participated. This event not only raises vital awareness for organ and tissue donation but also honours Brady's memory and the enduring impact of his life on family, friends, and those who received his precious gift of life.

tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I would like to acknowledge the Pak-Aus Engineers Association for their remarkable contribution to Australia's engineering community and for their ongoing commitment to excellence, mentorship, and multicultural collaboration. The Association continues to build strong professional and cultural bridges between Pakistani and Australian engineers, fostering innovation, opportunity, and shared growth. This year's annual function was a celebration of dedication and achievement, honouring those who have made outstanding contributions across their fields. Azhar Nasir, Behram Pestonji, Hamid Khan, Nabeel Khan, Shahid Javed, and Shakeel Ahmed were recognised for over 25 years of distinguished engineering service. Mr. Tariq Mahmood Mirza received the Lifetime Achievement Award for his contribution to Urdu literature, Dr. Ishrat Ali for community service, and Mr. Abdul Razzak Lakhani for engineering excellence. Distinguished Professor Dr. Rahat Munir, Consul General Mr. Qamar Zaman, and High Commissioner Mr. Irfan Shaukat were also honoured with Special Recognition Awards for their exceptional leadership and support. Led by President Insaf Khan and the executive committee, the Association exemplifies how professional expertise, cultural pride, and community service can come together to build a stronger, more connected Australia.

tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I would like to acknowledge the Pak-Aus Engineers Association for their remarkable contribution to Australia's engineering community and for their ongoing commitment to excellence, mentorship, and multicultural collaboration. The Association continues to build strong professional and cultural bridges between Pakistani and Australian engineers, fostering innovation, opportunity, and shared growth. This year's annual function was a celebration of dedication and achievement, honouring those who have made outstanding contributions across their fields. Azhar Nasir, Behram Pestonji, Hamid Khan, Nabeel Khan, Shahid Javed, and Shakeel Ahmed were recognised for over 25 years of distinguished engineering service. Mr. Tariq Mahmood Mirza received the Lifetime Achievement Award for his contribution to Urdu literature, Dr. Ishrat Ali for community service, and Mr. Abdul Razzak Lakhani for engineering excellence. Distinguished Professor Dr. Rahat Munir, Consul General Mr. Qamar Zaman, and High Commissioner Mr. Irfan Shaukat were also honoured with Special Recognition Awards for their exceptional leadership and support. Led by President Insaf Khan and the executive committee, the Association exemplifies how professional expertise, cultural pride, and community service can come together to build a stronger, more connected Australia.

tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —On behalf of my electorate of Badgerys Creek, I congratulate Oran Park Hockey Club for a very successful 2025 season, the most successful in its history. The club fielded 166 players across 15 teams, within various age groups, in the Metropolitan South West Association (MSWA) competition. Four of the club's teams qualified for the finals; the 3rd Grade Men, Under 12's Juniors, Under 10's Lightnings, and B Grade Ladies. Out of the four finalists, the Under 10's Lightnings and B Grade Ladies qualified for the Grand Finals, which were held on 26 September 2025. The club is to also be commended for its junior development, with 21 players participating in the MSWA Development carnivals and 11 players competing in the State Championships. I wish the club continued success as they look ahead to season 2026.

tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY LEONG ( Newtown ) —On behalf of the Newtown electorate, I would like to congratulate the Camdenville P&C Association for their successful 2025 Community Building Partnership grant and thank them for their work supporting the Camdenville Public School learning community. The P&C will use this grant to complete improvements to the school's outdoor learning space by installing platforms, a wobble bridge, and a log ladder. These improvements will ensure all students have access to an inclusive and fun playground area. Outdoor learning areas are crucial in ensuring that young people have access to a healthy and well-rounded education, supporting them to be active as young people and throughout their lives. I thank the Camdenville P&C Association for them commitment to ensuring that young people in our community have access to fun and inclusive outdoor areas for learning and play and acknowledge their tireless efforts supporting teachers and young learners in our community.

tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —Today I recognise Patsy Fry of Newport, whose creativity and persistence have brought colour and character to our Newport village. Patsy has lived in Newport for 30 years and has spent much of that time finding practical, community-minded ways to improve the place she loves. When she saw Newport needed more vibrancy, she took action, working with Northern Beaches Council to deliver the fairy lights that now brighten Robertson Road. More recently, Patsy has been the driving force behind Newport's unique stump planters. After seeing a tree removed on Queens Parade, she salvaged the stump, carved it by hand over 16 weeks and transformed it into a natural planter filled with geraniums. With support from generous locals, she has installed several more and is already working on the next set, hoping this becomes a defining feature for the village. Patsy also co-founded the Newport Sculpture Trail, engaging 35 local shops and bringing art, music and performance to the community. Patsy's passion, patience and commitment have left a lasting mark on Newport. I thank Patsy for her imagination, hard work and love for our community.

tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —I congratulate Middle Harbour Public School's Carnival for holding their Middle Harbour Public School Carnival. After a six-year hiatus, Middle Harbour Public School's P&C brought back the carnival, which is both a fundraiser and community event, and a must-attend event for all families and residents. Over 3,000 guests registered to attend, and the Carnival had a petting zoo, a giant slide, spinning tea cups, ponies and plenty of games for kids and adults to enjoy. There was great food on offer, including sausage sizzles and chips on a stick. There was also an assortment of craft goods and second-hand treasures to purchase. I acknowledge P&C President Dana Lightbody, Treasurer Andrea Voight, Secretary Carl Bunn and Committee Members Sarah Jarrett, Joanne De La Mar, and Carlotta Annan for their commitment and dedication, and for bringing back this iconic and well-loved event. I recognise Middle Harbour Public School Principal Laura Barry for her ongoing leadership and congratulate Middle Harbour Public School on their carnival.

tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES WALLACE ( Hornsby ) —I acknowledge and thank Studio ARTES for generously supplying this year's Christmas cards for our community. Studio ARTES has long been recognised for its outstanding work in providing creative programs, social connection and opportunities for people with disability. Their contribution of beautifully designed Christmas cards continues this tradition of creativity and community spirit. Each card features original artwork created by Studio ARTES artists Matthew Ye and Kate Beckerleg, whose talent and imagination shine through. Their vibrant underwater designs are filled with colourful fish, playful sea creatures and bold ocean scenes, bringing a sense of fun and creativity to the festive season. It is wonderful to see local artists sharing such joyful work with the community. Studio ARTES plays an important role in supporting individuals to express themselves, develop new skills and build confidence through the arts. I thank Studio ARTES, their dedicated staff and their talented artists for this thoughtful contribution. Their creativity brings our community together and adds a unique, uplifting touch to our celebrations during this festive season.

Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —I want to pay tribute to the remarkable volunteers of the Moorland Rural Fire Brigade, whose tireless efforts to protect our community reflect the highest standards of service and dedication. These individuals respond to bushfires, motor vehicle incidents, and severe weather emergencies, often working under dangerous conditions to safeguard lives and property across the Port Macquarie-Hastings and Mid Coast regions. Their contribution is not only brave—it is vital. The brigade plays a key role in strengthening local resilience, particularly during bushfire season. Beyond emergency response, they actively engage in community education and preparedness initiatives, helping residents stay informed and ready. They are often called away from the local area to support fire activities in other areas. The impact of their work reaches far beyond immediate safety. By reducing disaster risks and supporting recovery, they help protect local businesses, tourism, and infrastructure, while fostering unity and pride within our community. I commend Captain Stewart Waugh, Senior Deputy Captain Michael Hudson and every member of the Moorland Rural Fire Brigade for their unwavering commitment, bravery, and service. Their work strengthens our communities and ensures we are safer, better prepared, and more united in the face of adversity.

——————————
